sections.heading: 1. Draw the Funds-Flow Boundary Before Signing the First Merchant
paragraphs: Begin with a funds-flow diagram, not a salesperson's description of an ISO. Identify the merchant, acquiring bank, processor, gateway, independent sales organization, ATM owner, vault-cash provider, and settlement account owner. An operator that introduces merchants and receives contractual residuals occupies a different perimeter from one accepting customer money and forwarding it elsewhere. Under 31 CFR 1010.100(ff), money-transmitter status turns on actual activity and applicable exclusions, not the words used in a sales agreement. The payment-processor exclusion has specific conditions involving goods or services, a clearance and settlement system, and an agreement with the seller or creditor; an ISO label alone proves nothing. Keep merchant settlement directly between the acquiring arrangement and the merchant's designated account. Do not route proceeds through an ordinary operating account to simplify reconciliation. A software-only gateway may raise different questions from a wallet holding customer balances, while state money-transmission definitions and exemptions require separate analysis. Obtain the sponsor's written allocation of underwriting, monitoring, settlement, reserves, and complaints. Record whether registration is with a card network, a federal agency, or a state regulator; these are distinct requirements rather than interchangeable badges.

For a conventional withdrawal ATM, distinguish access to an existing bank account from accepting value for transmission. FinCEN guidance FIN-2007-G006 explains why the described limited-service ATM activity does not itself make the owner a money services business. That conclusion is activity-specific: cash deposits, crypto conversion, remittances, or stored-value loading change the analysis. Separately, 12 CFR 1005.16 requires an ATM operator imposing a covered fee to disclose that a fee will be imposed and its amount on screen or paper before the consumer commits, then obtain the consumer's election to continue. Federal law no longer requires the former exterior fee placard, although contracts or local requirements may add signage. Test the actual terminal sequence after every software or surcharge change; a photograph of the cabinet cannot establish screen compliance. Keep test receipts, firmware identifiers, deployment timestamps, and a documented cancel path. Regulation E error-resolution responsibilities under 12 CFR 1005.11 generally sit with the account-holding institution, but your contracts must route retrieval records and complaints promptly. A cash dispense reversal, partial dispense, or journal gap should create a service ticket before anyone treats the transaction as collectible revenue.

Treat sponsor-bank underwriting standards as operating obligations even where they exceed statutory minimums. The bank's customer identification and due-diligence duties under 31 CFR 1020.220 and 1010.230 do not automatically become identical direct duties of every referral agent; the sponsor agreement determines which collection and verification work the ISO performs. Use the sponsor's current checklist because exemptions and administrative relief can change required beneficial-owner collection. For high-risk MID orchestration, obtain written approval for the actual products, websites, owners, fulfillment model, and expected transaction patterns. Separate approved business lines only for genuine operating reasons, never to conceal common ownership, evade monitoring, or distribute prohibited transactions. Mastercard MATCH screening is a network process, not a state license, and an unfavorable result requires sponsor-directed review rather than identity substitution. OFAC screening, PCI DSS duties, and bank risk policies likewise have different legal and contractual sources. Record each source, responsible party, evidence requirement, and renewal interval in IRIS CRM. If the sponsor declines an activity, stop boarding that activity and offer an accurately described permitted alternative. Do not promise approval, unrestricted processing, or protection from reserves before underwriting is complete.

callout.title: Four Verifications Before Any Merchant or Terminal Goes Live
callout.body: Assign an evidence owner to each check. A sales promise, vendor badge, or unsigned application cannot substitute for the underlying record.

Match the merchant's owners, websites, product categories, and fulfillment practices to the sponsor's written underwriting approval before enabling production credentials.
Complete a credit, debit, prepaid, refund, and cancellation test suite for pricing; separately capture the ATM fee screen and consumer continuation sequence.
Execute the Schedule A, merchant authorization, venue agreement, and data-access terms with named signatories and a dated evidence package in IRIS CRM.

sections.heading: 2. Contract for Collectible Residuals, Transferable Rights, and Bounded Losses
paragraphs: Read Schedule A as a calculation specification. Define eligible merchant accounts, interchange and network assessments, processor buy rates, gateway charges, minimums, chargeback costs, reserve adjustments, and the residual split. State whether each percentage applies to merchant volume, gross markup, or a specified contribution pool. For illustration, $100,000 in monthly merchant card volume multiplied by a 0.40% contractual spread creates a $400 pool; a 70% ISO share produces $280 before any separately authorized adjustments. The $100,000 is not operator revenue. Require merchant-level statements with stable identifiers and enough fields to reproduce the calculation, including negative adjustments and their original transaction periods. Use IRIS CRM to compare expected residuals against remittances, but retain processor exports independently. Specify when earned amounts become payable, how long either party may dispute calculations, and whether the processor can alter buy rates unilaterally. An economically attractive spread is fragile if a general amendment clause can erase it without notice. Negotiate prospective notice, a documented objection mechanism, and defined treatment of existing merchants. For gateway markups, identify who provides the underlying service and who bears delivery obligations; that principal-versus-agent analysis matters when determining the operator's recognized revenue.

Protect the asset after termination. Define residual vesting, survival, merchant attrition treatment, reassignment, sale rights, successor servicing, and the narrow circumstances permitting forfeiture. An anti-circumvention clause should cover identified introductions and a reasonable attribution period, not claim every business in a region forever. Require a cure process for remediable breaches, while allowing immediate action for fraud or prohibited processing. Address liability caps, indemnity scope, exclusions, defense control, insurance, and dispute resolution together: a nominal cap offers little protection if every operational error falls into an unlimited exception. For ATM venues, specify exclusive placement boundaries, operating hours, electrical and network access, relocation rights, servicing access, theft allocation, cash ownership, and end-of-term removal. A $3.50 surcharge across 300 completed monthly withdrawals creates $1,050 in surcharge receipts. If the venue receives $0.75 per completed withdrawal, its $225 allocation leaves $825 before processor, connectivity, cash-service, and other expenses; describe this contract waterfall before deciding the accounting presentation. Vault cash remains a separate balance-sheet asset or provider obligation. If equipment or receivables secure an advance, identify collateral precisely and check the relevant state's UCC Article 9 attachment, perfection, and priority rules.

Preserve the canonical scorecard without smuggling client throughput into the top line. Formula v2.0 uses $90,000, $445,000, and $800,000 of annual retained operator revenue, despite the scorecard's gross-revenue label. These amounts already reflect the specified retained-share basis for ISO residuals, gateway markups, and ATM surcharges; do not apply another blanket residual split. At 30%, 42.5%, and 55% margins, owner net profits are exactly $27,000, $189,125, and $440,000. Corresponding annual operating costs are $63,000, $255,875, and $360,000. Teams remain 1 FT plus 3 contractors for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors for Scaled. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent conclusions depend on control of each specified service, not simply on which party issues an invoice. Reconcile contractual gross billings, pass-through allocations, recognized retained revenue, and operating expense in separate ledger columns. The stated $1,500–$10,000 monthly opex range is a planning reference, not a replacement for these scenario-implied total costs. Explain cost categories and stage differences rather than forcing a false reconciliation. Bounty cohorts are separate unit illustrations unless explicitly incorporated into a revised scorecard; adding their receipts to the canonical totals would change the supplied scenarios.

callout.title: Buy the Payment Waterfall, Not the Sales Deck
callout.body: Veteran operators preserve evidence at the same granularity as the fee formula. Rights that cannot be reconciled or transferred deserve a lower price.
items: Request three actual residual statements and reconstruct ten merchant calculations before accepting Schedule A; include one refund-heavy merchant and one account with negative adjustments.

Export merchant identifiers, venue contacts, fee-screen evidence, and residual audit fields monthly; never depend on continued vendor portal access after a contract dispute.

sections.heading: 3. Engineer State Pricing Rules and Optional Fintech Enrollment
paragraphs: Build pricing by transaction type and merchant location, not by a national sales slogan. A surcharge adds an amount because the customer uses an eligible credit card; a genuine cash discount reduces a clearly disclosed ordinary price. Calling an added checkout fee a discount does not change its mechanics. Visa and Mastercard rules prohibit surcharging their debit and prepaid transactions, including debit processed without a PIN. Maintain current acquirer-approved network caps, notice requirements, receipt fields, and eligible products as versioned configuration rather than hard-coded assumptions. Durbin's framework in 15 U.S.C. 1693o-2 and Regulation II addresses debit interchange, routing, and related network restrictions; it does not create universal permission for consumer debit surcharges. New York General Business Law 518 requires disclosure of the total credit-card price and restricts the surcharge relative to merchant cost. Massachusetts General Laws chapter 140D, section 28A prohibits seller credit-card surcharges while allowing qualifying discounts. California's surcharge statute has important litigation history, so do not treat its printed text as a complete enforcement answer. When a location's treatment is unresolved, retain ordinary disclosed pricing without a surcharge until the applicable state rule and sponsor policy are documented.

Sector differences can overwhelm a nominally attractive processing spread. Recurring subscriptions require a documented authorization path, cancellation mechanism, and accurate refund policy; online negative-option offers also implicate the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, 15 U.S.C. 8403. Travel, delayed delivery, advance ticket sales, and high-ticket services create fulfillment exposure that underwriting may address through reserves or delayed funding. Treat sponsor-approved merchant category coding as a description of reality, not a way to obtain cheaper risk treatment. Verifi RDR and Ethoca integrations can reduce dispute handling, but configure refund authority and duplicate-credit protection before enabling automated responses. A resolved alert does not erase deceptive sales or fix an undisclosed recurring charge. For interstate portfolios, record each physical location, checkout channel, customer-facing price display, and refund workflow. Test restaurants for tips and split tenders, unattended terminals for screen limitations, and ecommerce checkouts for debit recognition before the final price appears. If the gateway cannot reliably classify a card, do not surcharge that transaction. Ask the sponsor which state and network requirements apply to the actual arrangement; retain the answer with the deployment record. Escalate inconsistent vendor guidance instead of letting each sales contractor improvise a different interpretation.

For free_llc_fintech_bounty_stacking, define the offer as a $0-service-fee formation concierge: the founder pays mandatory state filing fees, while banking, corporate card, payroll, bookkeeping, and merchant referrals remain separately explained choices. The proposed 'Required Business Infrastructure Checklist' must distinguish actual statutory requirements from optional commercial recommendations; a referred account is not legally required merely because it pays a bounty. Disclose material referral relationships under the FTC endorsement framework and obtain separate authorization before sharing application data. Corporate cards remain subject to issuer underwriting, and payroll suitability depends on actual employees rather than bounty size. An illustrative ten-founder cohort averaging $1,000 in earned CPA awards produces $10,000, within the supplied $600–$1,800+ potential per formation. A modeled 15% reversal allowance leaves $8,500; $3,000 of attributable acquisition and servicing cost leaves $5,500 of cohort contribution, not canonical annual owner profit. Prequalify founders for genuine 30-day operating revenue intent, without manufacturing activity. If free operating-agreement and bookkeeping templates depend on verified bank funding, disclose that separate promotional condition upfront and offer an alternative without account enrollment. Use minimal verification, not bank passwords, and never withhold purchased filing work or required entity documents to force optional referrals.

sections.heading: 4. Use Verbatim Discovery Scripts and Preserve the Evidence Behind Every Claim
paragraphs: Open merchant conversations with permission and a bounded claim: 'We compare your current statement against a written processing proposal. With a redacted statement and your card mix, we can identify specific fee differences; we cannot quote your actual savings before that review. May I send the comparison checklist?' Follow with discovery rather than a surcharge pitch: 'Which states do you sell in, what share is debit, do you bill subscriptions, and how long after payment do customers receive the product?' Ask for masked statements through a secure upload, never full card numbers in email. For an ATM venue, use: 'We would propose a defined placement area, service responsibilities, and a commission per completed surcharge-bearing withdrawal. May we review foot traffic, access hours, existing exclusivity, and electrical availability before estimating transactions?' Do not convert foot traffic into guaranteed withdrawals. Commercial email must follow CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. Business recipients are not a blanket exemption. Keep a suppression list shared with authorized sending vendors so an exported lead file cannot silently revive an unsubscribed address.

Use a separate formation disclosure before collecting referral applications: 'Our formation service fee is $0; you pay the mandatory state filing fee. We may receive compensation if you choose eligible partner services. Bank, card, payroll, bookkeeping, and processing offers are optional, have separate terms, and may require qualification. Would you like the formation-only path or the optional referral checklist?' Then ask: 'What will the business sell during its first 30 operating days, when do you expect the first customer payment, and will you actually employ anyone?' This screens fit without instructing applicants to fabricate revenue. If a founder requests templates, say: 'The promotional template bundle requires verified funding of an eligible referred account; the separate terms explain the amount and timing. You can choose an alternative without opening that account, and your formation documents are unaffected.' State the actual funding amount and alternative before acceptance. For telephone outreach, evaluate 47 U.S.C. 227, 47 CFR 64.1200, applicable Telemarketing Sales Rule provisions, and state calling laws against the number type, dialing technology, message, and permission record. Do not assume that a business purpose permits prerecorded calls or marketing texts to a wireless number. Honor internal do-not-call requests immediately.

Make post-sale evidence collection part of the same workflow as prospecting. Each accepted proposal should reference its statement analysis, pricing version, state review, sponsor approval, executed agreement, and first settlement reconciliation. Record call permissions and disclosure versions without retaining unnecessary personal data; call recording itself requires review of applicable state permission rules. Restrict contractor access by role, prohibit local exports of payment credentials, and use processor tokens for operational references. Remote ATM telemetry should alert on cash levels, communications loss, dispenser faults, and unexplained transaction reversals, with an assigned escalation owner. Review bounty reversals, merchant attrition, negative residual adjustments, and unresolved disputes monthly. If a disclosure defect appears, pause the affected campaign or pricing feature, preserve records, correct customer-facing materials, and route remediation through the responsible provider. Do not erase logs to make conversion metrics look cleaner. Close the loop with a measured recovery plan: retest the affected terminal or checkout, confirm corrected enrollment language, and reconcile any resulting credits. The operator's advantage is a repeatable, documented service that survives an audit, staff turnover, or portfolio sale. Favor fewer correctly boarded accounts over a larger pipeline whose fees, permissions, or residual rights cannot be demonstrated.

sop_steps.title: Classify the activity and permitted outreach channel
sop_steps.action: Create the funds-flow map and record the merchant, venue, or founder's actual operating facts.
sop_steps.detail: Identify applicable states, transaction types, account custody, sponsor duties, and outreach permissions. Assign unresolved transmission or calling questions to a named reviewer before using the affected activity or channel.

sop_steps.title: Execute the economic and data-rights documents
sop_steps.action: Sign the relevant Schedule A, venue terms, referral disclosures, and narrowly scoped data permissions.
sop_steps.detail: Document fee triggers, deductions, residual survival, ownership boundaries, liability allocation, dispute procedures, and export rights. Store the executed version alongside a reproducible unit-economics worksheet.

sop_steps.title: Test the actual customer-facing implementation
sop_steps.action: Run transaction and enrollment tests against the deployed screen, receipt, checkout, and script versions.
sop_steps.detail: Include debit, prepaid, credit, refund, cancellation, ATM fee election, and formation-only enrollment paths. Disable any affected feature that fails, retain evidence, and repeat the test after correction.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile earned revenue and ongoing exceptions
sop_steps.action: Match the first settlement and each monthly residual or bounty statement to its contractual calculation.
sop_steps.detail: Track reversals, credits, attrition, opt-outs, terminal faults, and unresolved disputes. Keep customer throughput and vault cash outside operator revenue, and compare actual retained earnings against the unchanged canonical cases.

chapters.pull_quote: A payment portfolio is worth the residuals you can reconcile and the rights you can enforce.
action_checklist: Draw separate merchant, ATM, and fintech referral funds-flow maps; identify custody, settlement ownership, and the federal and state activity boundaries for each.
Reconstruct a Schedule A residual calculation and an ATM venue waterfall from source statements, preserving retained revenue separately from merchant volume and vault cash.
Negotiate fee triggers, residual survival, assignment, anti-circumvention, liability allocation, dispute procedures, and usable data exports before committing acquisition capital.
Build a location-specific pricing register and test credit, debit, prepaid, refunds, and ATM fee disclosures against current sponsor requirements and applicable state law.
Deploy the formation-only enrollment path, referral compensation disclosures, exact promotional funding terms, and minimally intrusive bounty verification without forced account registration.
Load the approved outreach scripts, suppression records, four-step SOP, and monthly exception review into IRIS CRM with named owners and independently retained evidence.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #32, ISO Payment Processing & ATM Arbitrage, ranks #02 of 36 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps 12 operator plays into one evidence-led automation system: source qualified accounts, board through sponsor-controlled workflows, reconcile retained residuals, resolve eligible disputes, monitor ATM liquidity, and recycle verified results into distribution. A 1 FT + 3 C team targets 70%+ repetitive-task automation without delegating underwriting, pricing exceptions, cash movement, or consequential communications to an LLM. The canonical annual owner-profit cases remain $27,000 Conservative, $189,125 Base, and $440,000 Scaled. Each workflow carries a unit-cost budget, a replay-safe event record, a named reviewer, and a manual fallback. Growth follows measured contribution and service capacity rather than merchant settlement volume, vault cash, or speculative rewards.

sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence pipeline before automating merchant decisions
paragraphs: Start with a Python service that receives only contract-authorized processor, CRM, dispute-provider, and ATM-monitoring events. IRIS CRM capabilities depend on the purchased service and partner permissions; inspect the actual integration contract rather than assuming every boarding field or residual report has a public endpoint. Where webhooks are unavailable, ingest scheduled encrypted exports through the same event envelope. Store event_id, source, merchant reference, received_at, schema_version, payload_digest, and processing_state. Validate signatures using the provider's documented algorithm, enforce timestamp tolerance where supported, and reject duplicate event keys before creating work. Python's hashlib, hmac, json, sqlite3, and decimal support a small prototype; SQLite requires deliberate single-writer handling and a tested migration path before multiple workers contend. Persist the authenticated event before acknowledging receipt, then let a worker perform transformations outside the request lifecycle. Separate immutable source evidence from normalized records and proposed actions. A revised Schedule A must create a new effective-dated version, never overwrite the version that explained last month's payout. This architecture makes a late processor correction replayable without accidentally resubmitting a merchant application or issuing a second refund. Assign one owner to every connector and record its last successful synchronization.

Use the LLM as a constrained extraction and drafting component, not as the ledger or sponsor underwriter. Supply redacted documents with explicit field definitions, require structured output, and validate every amount, date, currency, and identifier against deterministic rules. Keep full card numbers, security codes, PIN material, bank credentials, and customer authentication secrets outside prompts and general application logs. Merchant websites and uploaded statements are untrusted evidence: instructions embedded inside them cannot change tool permissions, recipient addresses, or pricing rules. For a boarding packet, the model may identify a missing ownership document and draft a request; the responsible contractor checks the cited source before sending anything consequential. Sponsor-bank underwriting remains with the authorized decision maker, especially for elevated-risk categories and adverse history. Do not rotate MIDs to conceal activity, bypass restrictions, or fragment chargeback ratios. Maintain separate permissions for reading evidence, proposing updates, and executing approved changes. The full-time operator owns commercial exceptions; three contractors cover boarding, residual analysis, and field-service coordination under restricted accounts. Use a weekly sample of ordinary completed cases as well as every exception to catch silent extraction drift before it becomes a portfolio-wide billing error.

Define the automation denominator before advertising a seventy-percent result. An illustrative weekly cohort contains 1,000 eligible repetitive work items: 300 research records, 200 qualification checks, 180 boarding completeness checks, 140 residual lines, 100 telemetry alerts, and 80 distribution drafts. If 720 finish their defined low-risk endpoint without human editing, straight-through completion is 72%; the other 280 remain assisted or manual. A generated application is not completed underwriting, and a draft email is not a sent acquisition touch. Keep these endpoints separate in the dashboard. Assume each automated item formerly required four minutes and now creates twenty seconds of average review or monitoring work: 720 times 220 seconds equals 44 hours saved before maintenance. At an illustrative $0.012 model charge, $0.003 queue and storage allocation, and $0.005 monitoring allocation, each successful run costs $0.020; 720 runs cost $14.40. Add retries, failed attempts, subscriptions, integration upkeep, and reviewer labor separately. Count all attempts in the cost numerator and only accepted outputs in the completion denominator. Stop increasing throughput when exception aging rises, even if token costs remain tiny. The bottleneck is accountable review capacity, not inexpensive text generation.

callout.title: Make source evidence cheaper to retrieve than an argument
callout.body: The strongest small-team advantage is a short path from an alert to the exact contract, transaction, or machine record that explains it.
items: Store the Schedule A version and processor statement page beside each residual exception; a payout total alone cannot explain a basis-point change.
Treat a successful HTTP response as transport evidence only; require the provider's durable transaction reference before marking a refund or boarding submission complete.
Compare ATM dispense journals with host records and physical balancing; a healthy communications heartbeat does not prove usable cash availability.
Track duplicate dispute alerts across contracted providers by original transaction identity before any refund, while preserving each provider's separate deadline.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile automation economics to retained revenue, not payment volume
paragraphs: Anchor every dashboard to the Formula v2.0 revenue basis: net retained ISO processing residuals, gateway markups, and ATM surcharges. The scorecard labels the annual top line gross revenue, but it is not merchant card settlement volume or ATM vault cash. Conservative revenue of $90,000 less $63,000 total modeled expenses produces $27,000 owner profit at 30%. Base revenue of $445,000 less $255,875 produces $189,125 at 42.5%. Scaled revenue of $800,000 less $360,000 produces $440,000 at 55%, with staffing increasing from 1 FT plus 3 C to 2 FT plus 4 C. These expense totals are algebraic reconciliations of the supplied cases, not newly estimated contractor budgets. Keep the stated $1,500–$10,000 monthly operating-expense range separate from a complete scenario expense bridge; it does not explain every modeled annual cost. Similarly, $8,000–$45,000 startup capital is a funding requirement, not recognized revenue. For an agent arrangement, apply the documented retained share consistently with the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment. If $20,000 of statement economics leaves the operator a contractual 35% share, the modeled retained amount is $7,000, not $20,000 followed by a second retained-share deduction. Record timing differences separately from entitlement differences so cash receipts cannot silently redefine earned revenue.

Residual automation should recompute expected earnings from authorized source fields, not infer interchange from merchant-facing labels. Suppose an illustrative account generates $80,000 eligible monthly card volume and the signed arrangement leaves eight basis points plus a $15 retained gateway markup: $80,000 times 0.0008 plus $15 equals $79 monthly retained revenue. A two-basis-point unexplained reduction costs $16 monthly, or $192 annually if volume remains constant. Compare actual statements to effective dates, exclusions, minimums, and contractual adjustments before calling that difference leakage. Dispute automation needs a separate transaction-level economic test. Verifi RDR rules and Ethoca alert handling depend on the specific contracted product, enrollment, and response mechanics; neither name implies universal protection against chargebacks. For an illustrative $40 eligible transaction, compare a $40 refund plus provider fees with the expected disputed principal, dispute fee, recovery probability, and operational cost under the merchant's policy. Avoid counting avoided fees as operator revenue. Match prior refunds and transaction identity before acting, retain the provider reference, and reconcile subsequent processor postings. If eligibility is unclear or a provider times out, create a deadline-bearing human task rather than retrying a potentially completed refund without checking its status.

Map agency_ad_spend_card_multiplier_rebate_cycling to TRACK_2 only for genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements. The full play is Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling. An illustrative $100,000 monthly advertising budget earns $1,500 in contract-permitted rewards at 1.5% and $200 in a separately permitted 0.2% volume rebate. Subtract $600 funding cost, $300 processing cost, and $500 client pass-through obligations: incremental contribution is $300, before other applicable expenses. At twelve identical months, that is $3,600, not $1.2 million of operator revenue. Do not add this illustration to the canonical scorecard cases; its inclusion requires an explicitly reconciled portfolio allocation. Value points at realizable contractual redemption economics, not travel-blog valuations, and determine the appropriate accounting treatment separately. A Python eligibility ledger should track issuer terms, merchant category, spend caps, client authorization, payment due dates, rebate reversals, and the party entitled to each benefit. The operator reviews any reward-dependent recommendation. Prohibit fabricated purchases, circular transfers, and spend created solely to manufacture rewards. When issuer eligibility changes or the funding spread turns negative, move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending. Automation monitors the spread; it never creates permission to use a client's money.

callout.body: Pre-flight verification applies to the action being taken, not merely to the account's previous acceptance.
items: Confirm the sponsor-approved business category, actual activity, and merchant identity before boarding or changing processing arrangements; never use another MID to evade restrictions.

sections.heading: 3. Turn verified service results into repeatable distribution
paragraphs: Build the distribution flywheel around a closed service fact: a corrected residual calculation, a faster complete boarding packet, or improved ATM availability supported by logs. Ask the merchant or venue for permission before using identifiable results, then create a short reviewed case study with the measurement window, denominator, and material limitations. A programmatic page generator can assemble vertical-specific education from approved components: restaurant gateway reconciliation, independent-retailer pricing comparisons, or venue cash-service planning. It must not manufacture local offices, customer endorsements, savings claims, or sponsor relationships. Require a unique practical example and a source-backed operating answer before publishing each page. Use Search Console and first-party analytics to attribute qualified inquiries, then link the resulting CRM opportunity to its eventual retained contribution. Eighty weekly distribution drafts at the earlier two-cent run budget cost $1.60 in variable automation expense, but editorial review and distribution costs still matter. If ten qualified inquiries require $200 of total production and review, cost per qualified inquiry is $20. Only signed, activated, economically acceptable accounts advance the acquisition scorecard. A page generating traffic without accepted opportunities is a research signal, not a profitable distribution asset. Retire duplicated pages instead of expanding a weak template across hundreds of locations.

Outbound should be a research-to-conversation system rather than a message volume contest. Build narrowly defined lists from permitted sources, deduplicate company and contact records, and document why the offering fits each prospect. An LLM can turn a verified observation into a concise draft, but it cannot invent a processor relationship or claim to have audited a statement it has never seen. Under 15 U.S.C. § 7704, commercial email requires accurate transmission information, nondeceptive subjects, the applicable advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out mechanism; honor opt-outs within the statutory period and suppress them across vendors. Telephone and text campaigns need separate analysis under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and implementing rules before activation. Keep the default workflow email-only until the proposed additional channel has been reviewed. In an illustrative cohort, 400 relevant messages produce twenty replies, eight qualified calls, four complete applications, and two activated merchants. If total acquisition effort costs $600, acquisition cost is $300 per activated merchant. At $79 monthly retained revenue, revenue-only payback is about 3.8 months; contribution payback takes longer after servicing costs and attrition. Track both instead of presenting the shorter number as recovered cash profit.

Referrals and venue partnerships compound only when service capacity keeps pace with promises. Trigger a referral request after a verified positive service event and an account-owner review, not immediately after an automated satisfaction score. For ATM venues, use uptime, successful dispenses, cash-out hours, and reconciled surcharge sharing as the shared operating record. A venue with 400 monthly withdrawals and $1 retained contribution per withdrawal contributes $400 before unallocated overhead; a proposed $150 monthly exclusivity payment leaves $250 before those remaining costs. Do not confuse the withdrawn principal with sales. Offer reporting access that exposes only that venue's records, and restrict referral attribution links so they reveal no merchant account details. For pricing-led campaigns, distinguish a credit-card surcharge from a genuine cash discount or clearly displayed dual pricing. Card-brand rules, debit restrictions, sponsor requirements, and applicable state law must be evaluated against the actual implementation, not its marketing label. New York General Business Law § 518 makes displayed total credit pricing especially relevant there; do not transplant a national template without checking jurisdiction. When pricing evidence becomes stale, pause affected content and offers while continuing ordinary service and nonpricing educational outreach. Distribution should amplify verified operations, not conceal operational debt.

sections.heading: 4. Scale with bounded actions, cash controls, and rehearsed recovery
paragraphs: ATM telemetry deserves a separate control plane because monitoring a machine is not authority to move cash. Collect timestamped cassette estimates, dispense counts, reject counts, communications status, and electronic-journal references from the authorized monitoring arrangement. Reconcile estimated cash against host transactions and physical balancing; dispense reversals and partial dispenses can break a simplistic counter. For an illustrative site holding $6,000 usable cash with expected withdrawals of $1,500 daily, nominal coverage is four days. With two days of replenishment lead time and a one-day safety buffer, issue an alert when usable cash reaches $4,500, adjusted for weekends and known events. The field contractor confirms conditions, while the authorized custodian approves cash movement through established procedures. Under 12 CFR § 1005.16, a fee-charging ATM operator must provide the required fee notice on screen or paper before the consumer is committed and allow the consumer to elect to continue. Verify the actual terminal experience after configuration changes. FinCEN treatment depends on the actual services performed; do not assume conventional withdrawal-only ATM operation and additional money-transmission services have identical obligations. Keep the bank relationship, source-of-cash records, terminal configuration history, and service permissions aligned with the actual business model.

Design failures as explicit states: received, validated, proposed, authorized, submitted, confirmed, reconciled, or held. A provider timeout after submission is an uncertain outcome, not proof that nothing happened. Before retrying a refund or application submission, query the documented status mechanism or obtain provider confirmation. Where supported, reuse the original idempotency key; where unsupported, require manual resolution before another consequential request. Retry temporary read failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, then move exhausted work into a dead-letter queue carrying the original event reference and a named owner. Do not retry authentication failures indefinitely or log secrets while debugging them. Monitor oldest unresolved item, duplicate-action count, reconciliation variance, stale telemetry minutes, and reviewer queue age. Set initial targets from actual contractual deadlines and service commitments, not arbitrary dashboard colors. Every day, compare counts and financial totals between source reports and processed records to detect missing events that error logs cannot reveal. Maintain encrypted backups, restricted restoration credentials, and a tested restore procedure. A replay drill should recover records without reissuing external actions. An incident is closed only when operational state, provider state, and ledger state agree, with the reconciliation evidence attached to the incident record.

Scale distribution only after the exception system survives a controlled load test using synthetic or appropriately de-identified records. Double research and draft volume first, hold consequential action limits constant, and measure accepted outputs, reviewer minutes, provider errors, and downstream activation. In the Base case, the full-time operator retains pricing and relationship accountability while the three contractors maintain boarding, residual, and field-service queues. In the Scaled case, the second full-time role can own operations and quality, with four contractors supporting the documented workload. Those roles explain coverage, not a new profit forecast: the canonical $800,000 revenue and $440,000 owner profit remain unchanged. Review access when responsibilities change, revoke departed-user credentials promptly, and separate production secrets from development examples. Each week, inspect all high-impact exceptions and a stratified sample of ordinary automated completions across processors, merchant categories, venues, and acquisition sources. Track false passes separately from false holds because their consequences differ. If automation falls below the measured 70% target, fix the largest repetitive exception class rather than removing necessary review. The durable flywheel is better evidence producing fewer exceptions, faster service, stronger referrals, and more retained contribution per reviewer hour. Keep that loop measurable even when acquisition volume temporarily slows.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 3 C (4 people) -> 2 FT + 4 C (6 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #32, ISO Payment Processing & ATM Arbitrage, ranks #02 of 36 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 12 mapped plays need one accountable operating system, not twelve disconnected businesses. Start with one full-time owner and three specialist contractors; expand to two full-time seats and four contractors only when verified residual contribution funds the added capacity. Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits are $27,000, $189,125, and $440,000, respectively. This chapter assigns merchant acquisition, boarding, residual reconciliation, and ATM field work; ties compensation to collected, durable contribution; and establishes weekly evidence standards. Transferable contracts, clean cohorts, documented intellectual-property ownership, and customer and counterparty concentration at or below 25% support either a credible sale process or a durable cash-producing portfolio.

sections.heading: 1. Assign twelve play lanes to four accountable seats
paragraphs: Build the starting pod around one full-time owner, one acquisition contractor, one boarding and residual-control contractor, and one ATM field-service contractor. The owner retains sponsor relationships, commercial exceptions, treasury authority, and final underwriting submissions; the sponsor makes its own underwriting decisions. For this operating design, organize the volume's twelve mapped plays into explicit execution lanes rather than implying that separate businesses require separate hires: wholesale Schedule A negotiation, conventional merchant placement, properly disclosed dual pricing, gateway markup attachment, approved high-risk placement, dispute deflection, residual recovery, retention and repricing, exclusive ATM venue acquisition, ATM deployment, telemetry-led service, and surcharge optimization. These are working lane labels, not additional scorecard revenue categories. Route every opportunity through IRIS CRM using merchant or terminal identifiers, sponsor ownership, signed commercial terms, and a named accountable seat. High-risk MID orchestration means matching disclosed activity to sponsor-approved processing arrangements, never cycling identities around monitoring or termination. Give contractors the minimum access their deliverables require; nobody needs unrestricted merchant exports merely to schedule a terminal installation. The owner should see one exception queue, not twelve inboxes. Maintain a written backup for each critical function so a contractor absence does not interrupt settlements, incident response, or venue service.

Use deliverable-based contractor agreements with scope, pricing, evidence, response windows, confidentiality, and termination assistance. A label alone does not establish independent-contractor status; examine actual control, economic dependence, and applicable state tests before imposing employee-style schedules or exclusivity. As an illustrative acquisition arrangement, pay $150 after an approved merchant produces its first reconciled residual, then 10% of that merchant's eligible collected contribution for twelve months. Define contribution after contractually senior processor deductions and specified direct servicing costs, and exclude taxes, merchant settlements, reserves, and vault cash. Document treatment of reversals and post-termination commissions rather than inventing clawbacks after a dispute. The boarding specialist can quote a monthly capacity retainer plus accepted-file fees; the field contractor can quote scheduled visits, emergency dispatch, and parts separately. Require a complete boarding packet within two business days of receiving complete inputs, a critical ATM alert acknowledgment within thirty minutes during purchased coverage, and geographically realistic restoration targets. These are proposed service terms, not universal industry standards. Pay accepted invoices against evidence, while rejecting only documented defects under the agreement. Contractor compensation must fit the scenario expense envelope; it cannot become an extra deduction below the stated owner profit.

At scale, keep the founder as the first full-time seat and add an operations lead as the second. Retain acquisition, boarding and residual control, and ATM field service as three contractor seats; add an independent bookkeeping and quality assurance contractor as the fourth. Six people still operate all twelve lanes, but the operations lead owns queue throughput and coverage while the independent reviewer tests collections, access changes, and payout calculations. At four people, the owner performs that review and buys only bounded specialist engagements inside the existing contractor scopes. Do not represent a contractor firm's unlimited technicians as six named people; disclose subcontractor dependencies and their costs separately. Hire against trailing workload, quality failures, and cash coverage rather than forecasted merchant volume. A useful planning trigger is eight consecutive weeks of excessive service backlog despite documented automation, paired with six months of funded incremental seat cost. Make the hiring calculation after replacement coverage and working-capital needs. Customer relationships, sponsor permissions, equipment records, and operating instructions belong in company-controlled systems. The owner should be able to take a two-week absence without becoming the emergency password vault or sole interpreter of a residual statement.

callout.title: Protect the residual before rewarding the activity
callout.body: The best contractor scorecards make durable collections easier to verify than optimistic activity reports.
items: Store each sponsor's effective Schedule A version beside the merchant cohort; audit changes against the version that actually governed the statement period.
Delay activation incentives until the first residual reconciles; a boarded MID with no eligible processing is not a productive acquisition.
Link ATM dispatch invoices to terminal IDs, alert timestamps, fault codes, and restoration evidence so repeat visits reveal unresolved causes.
Require a second reviewer for contractor bank-detail changes, and verify the change using an established contact channel rather than the requesting email.

sections.heading: 2. Run a weekly evidence scorecard and enforce concentration limits
paragraphs: Close the weekly operating scorecard every Monday using a dated snapshot rather than a live dashboard that silently changes after the meeting. The owner reviews collected retained revenue, accrued retained revenue, active revenue-producing merchants, merchant retention, residual yield, gateway attachment, dispute exceptions, ATM availability, service backlog, and concentration. Define an active merchant as one generating an eligible residual during the measurement period; report approved but inactive MIDs separately. Calculate revenue retention on the opening merchant cohort, separating churn, repricing, volume changes, and recovered billing errors. A weekly view can flag movements, while monthly and trailing-quarter views absorb statement timing. Express merchant yield as retained ISO revenue divided by eligible processed volume, multiplied by 10,000 basis points; that denominator is activity, never recognized operator revenue. For ATMs, report retained surcharge contribution per completed withdrawal and availability during contracted venue hours. Exclude planned venue closure only when the service agreement supports that treatment, and show the exclusion. Assign every red metric an owner, a dated correction, and evidence needed for closure. Track backlog age alongside ticket count so clearing easy tickets cannot conceal an unresolved settlement discrepancy or stranded terminal.

Set a portfolio policy that no customer group and no processor or sponsor dependency contributes more than 25% of trailing-twelve-month retained revenue. Apply the same ceiling to prospective acquired portfolios before funding, and calculate it on combined books after closing. Group related merchant entities under common control; group venue contracts controlled by the same landlord or hospitality operator. For counterparties, inspect the underlying sponsor and processing chain because several reseller brands can share one failure point. If dependencies overlap, test each exposure independently rather than forcing all categories to sum to 100%. Four equal independent relationships barely satisfy a 25% ceiling and provide no growth buffer, so aim below 20% when practical. Early portfolios may mathematically fail this policy; flag that exception openly and restrict distributions or additional concentrated growth until diversification catches up. Do not claim that dividing a merchant into additional MIDs diversifies exposure. Add a contribution-based concentration view because a low-revenue venue can produce disproportionate profit. Measure vault-cash provider and field-service dependencies separately using cash exposure and covered-terminal counts, with backup arrangements rather than misleading revenue percentages. Document remediation owners and actual alternative capacity.

Make contractor quality measurable without pretending that every operating metric has a statutory threshold. Target at least 98% first-pass completeness on boarding files, reconciliation of every received monthly residual statement within five business days, and zero unexplained contractor payout differences older than thirty days. These are internal operating targets. Dispute and fraud thresholds must come from the currently applicable sponsor and card-brand program, with internal warning levels set sufficiently earlier to permit action. Use Verifi RDR and Ethoca only where enrolled and supported; measure resolved cases, refunded dollars, vendor fees, and duplicate credits rather than celebrating an unqualified deflection count. A refund can prevent escalation while still reducing contribution. For ATM service, distinguish communications outages, dispenser faults, cash exhaustion, and venue access failures because each requires a different remedy and responsible party. Sample installed pricing screens and merchant-facing receipts after configuration changes. Debit and prepaid transactions must not be swept into credit-card surcharge configurations, and state restrictions need a maintained location matrix. MATCH-related screening and escalation belong with authorized sponsor processes; the pod must never market another MID as a way around a termination. Keep evidence available for review without storing sensitive authentication data.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the weekly evidence set
sop_steps.action: Export IRIS CRM queues, processor statement updates, ATM alerts, and bank receipts into a dated company-controlled folder.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve source identifiers and extraction times; separate monthly statement lag from genuine operational deterioration.

sop_steps.action: Bridge accruals to collections, refresh cohort retention, and recalculate customer and counterparty exposure.
sop_steps.detail: The preparing contractor records assumptions; the owner or independent reviewer tests material differences and payout changes.

sop_steps.action: Hold a thirty-minute owner-led review that assigns one accountable seat and completion date to each material exception.
sop_steps.detail: Use sponsor-specific escalation thresholds, venue response commitments, and the 25% exposure policy rather than improvised judgments.

sections.heading: 3. Build accrual books and transferable contractual rights
paragraphs: Treat the scorecard's gross revenue label as the supplied operator-revenue total on a net retained basis, not merchant gross billings. Conservative revenue of $90,000 less $63,000 of modeled expenses produces $27,000 owner profit at 30%. Base revenue of $445,000 less $255,875 produces $189,125 at 42.5%. Scaled revenue of $800,000 less $360,000 produces $440,000 at 55%. Keep the stated teams attached to those cases: one full-time seat plus three contractors for Conservative and Base, and two full-time seats plus four contractors for Scaled. The corresponding monthly revenue averages are $7,500, approximately $37,083.33, and approximately $66,666.67. They are annual averages, not promises of smooth monthly collections. The separate $1,500–$10,000 monthly operating range is a planning reference, not a ceiling on all expenses in the larger modeled cases; base and scaled implied total expenses exceed it. Document the scope difference instead of forcing the numbers to fit. Under ASC 606, evaluate principal-versus-agent presentation for each performance obligation. The supplied retained-revenue basis must not receive another invented retained-share haircut. Merchant settlement funds and ATM vault cash remain outside recognized operator revenue and owner profit.

Create separate ledger accounts for ISO residuals, gateway markups, ATM surcharges, receivables, sponsor reserves, contractor commissions, venue payments, field service, software, and cash-custody balances where applicable. Record earned residuals using contract terms and supported estimates when statements arrive after month-end, then true up against actual statements. Distinguish a collectible timing difference from a disputed receivable that requires an allowance or write-off under the accounting policy. Preserve the bridge from gross statement components through contractual deductions to retained operator revenue. If a venue share or upstream commission already reduces the reported retained amount, do not expense it again. Conversely, commissions incurred by the operator and not already netted belong in expenses. Maintain merchant and terminal cohorts by activation month, acquisition source, sponsor, venue group, contract version, and cancellation rights. Review three-, six-, and twelve-month contribution after direct servicing costs, not just headline processing volume. Reconcile terminal transaction counts, surcharge rates, reversals, and venue splits to cash receipts. Vault cash movements need their own ownership and custody reconciliation; cash dispensed is not a service expense merely because it leaves a cassette. Support every material estimate with a preparer, reviewer, source document, and subsequent settlement check.

Transferability begins before the first contractor receives system access. Obtain signed intellectual-property assignments for original scripts, training materials, configuration documentation, and other copyrightable deliverables; 17 U.S.C. section 204(a) generally requires a signed writing for a copyright ownership transfer. Do not assume every commissioned work qualifies as work made for hire. Inventory pre-existing contractor tools and obtain licenses broad enough for continued operation and the contemplated transaction. Keep domains, telemetry accounts, CRM administration, vendor subscriptions, and recovery credentials under company control, subject to vendor transfer terms. Merchant agreements, ISO contracts, and venue leases require separate review of assignment, change of control, termination, residual survival, exclusivity, and solicitation restrictions. UCC section 9-408 can limit certain restrictions affecting security interests, but it does not generally compel a counterparty to accept a buyer's performance or provide system access. Capture required consents as named transaction dependencies, not assumed rights. Maintain ATM disclosure evidence under 12 CFR 1005.16, including the fee amount presented before commitment and the consumer's election to continue. Evaluate actual ATM activities against FinCEN's money-services-business definitions; cash dispensing alone does not establish that every operator is a money transmitter.

sections.heading: 4. Price transferable cash flow, then choose sale or continued ownership
paragraphs: Use valuation ranges as negotiating models, not claims about current transaction comparables. An illustrative small owner-operated book might be evaluated at two to four times normalized annual seller discretionary earnings; an illustrative residual-stream proposal might quote twenty-four to thirty-six times eligible monthly residual contribution. These bases are different and must never be added together for the same cash flow. Buyers define eligible residuals differently, sometimes before servicing costs, so reconstruct the actual purchased economics from the term sheet. Applying the earnings sensitivity mechanically to Base owner profit of $189,125 gives $378,250–$756,500 before normalization. Conservative yields $54,000–$108,000, and Scaled yields $880,000–$1,760,000. These are illustrative enterprise-value sensitivities, not equity proceeds or verified market prices. Owner profit is not automatically EBITDA or seller discretionary earnings: reconcile owner compensation, recurring labor, taxes, interest, depreciation, and claimed add-backs before selecting a basis. A buyer needing an additional $90,000 annual replacement operator would reduce the Base earnings basis to $99,125 only if that replacement cost is not already captured. At the same illustrative range, that adjusted basis supports $198,250–$396,500. Operational independence is therefore an earnings issue, not cosmetic documentation.

Build a buyer data room that follows money from each surviving contract to each collected dollar. Include twenty-four months of statements where available, monthly accrual bridges, cohort retention, sponsor pricing history, dispute outcomes, concentration analysis, terminal ownership, venue rights, contractor agreements, intellectual-property assignments, and security incident records. For a younger portfolio, disclose the shorter operating history and price that uncertainty rather than manufacturing a full track record. Segment high-risk merchants, short-dated venue contracts, terminable residual arrangements, and accounts awaiting sponsor consent. A buyer can then exclude, discount, or condition those assets explicitly. Define earnouts using named cohorts, collected eligible residuals, allowed deductions, reporting access, dispute procedures, and treatment of buyer-directed repricing. Otherwise, a headline multiple can conceal an uncollectible deferred balance. Distinguish enterprise value from equity proceeds by addressing debt, transaction costs, working-capital adjustments, escrows, and separately owned cash. Do not sell a cash-loading provider's vault cash as company property. Release detailed merchant information only through authorized diligence channels with appropriate access restrictions. Transfer of a customer relationship does not automatically authorize unrestricted movement of payment credentials or vendor-controlled data. Stage access, log downloads, and revoke permissions when a bidder exits.

A premium requires reduced uncertainty that a buyer can verify: durable residual rights, consent-ready assignments, diversified relationships, stable cohorts, and a pod that works without founder intervention. Test that claim with a documented two-week owner absence before considering a sale, while preserving emergency authority and sponsor-required contacts. The same discipline supports a cash-cow strategy. Compare after-tax sale proceeds and reinvestment alternatives with realistic future distributions after replacement labor, equipment refresh, working capital, and adverse attrition. Do not simply divide enterprise value by unadjusted owner profit and call the result a payback period. Stress the loss of the largest permitted customer and largest processor dependency separately, then test their joint loss where correlated. At a 25% revenue exposure, lost profit depends on avoidable costs and contractual survival, not a flat 25% reduction in earnings. Keep the twelve lanes visible during this exercise: acquisition and pricing create revenue, approved boarding and dispute operations protect continuity, residual controls protect collections, and exclusive venues plus reliable ATM service sustain local economics. Sell when the offered risk-adjusted proceeds outperform continued ownership on your documented assumptions; retain when the pod reliably produces cash without hidden founder labor or concentrated fragility.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #32, ISO Payment Processing & ATM Arbitrage, holds Rank #02 of 36 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint translates its 12 mapped plays into a controlled launch for one full-time operator and three contractors: prove sponsor access, document retained spreads, board approved merchants, and validate exclusive ATM locations before expanding. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $27,000 Conservative, $189,125 Base, and $440,000 Scaled; none is a first-month target. Days 1–30 establish evidence, with a $6,000 operating cash-deployment ceiling and separate vault cash. Day-30/60/90 decisions distinguish fatal sponsorship or authorization failures from repairable conversion problems and genuinely repeatable contribution. Scale follows reconciled economics, not merchant settlement volume, signed applications, or optimistic ATM footfall.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Establish Sponsor Access, Twelve Play IDs, and a Cash Boundary
paragraphs: Start Day 1 by making the twelve plays explicit workstreams rather than twelve simultaneous launches. This chapter's operating map is P01 wholesale Schedule A negotiation; P02 interchange-plus merchant acquisition; P03 gateway markup attachment; P04 permitted credit-card surcharge deployment; P05 genuine dual-pricing deployment; P06 sponsor-approved higher-risk MID placement; P07 residual audit recovery; P08 retention and repricing; P09 Verifi RDR or Ethoca dispute deflection; P10 exclusive ATM venue acquisition; P11 ATM surcharge yield management; and P12 telemetry and vault-cash control. These are operating labels for the twelve mapped plays, not twelve independent revenue forecasts. Activate P01, P02, P03, P07, P10, and P12 first; the remaining plays require an eligible merchant, actual dispute exposure, a renewal opportunity, or measured ATM traffic. Assign the full-time operator forty weekly hours across selling, sponsor coordination, and decisions. Contractor one receives eight hours for boarding and evidence control; contractor two receives six for integrations and terminal configuration; contractor three receives six for ATM field service and cash-provider coordination. That sixty-hour weekly pod must also handle support. Reserve twelve of those hours for exceptions, and stop adding installations whenever unresolved incidents consume that reserve. No contractor receives unrestricted merchant banking access.

Use Days 2–4 to replace attractive sales language with enforceable economics. Request the sponsor or upstream ISO agreement, current Schedule A, residual ownership and vesting language, termination treatment, reserve rights, clawbacks, and the actual underwriting checklist. Confirm who registers the business with each relevant card network and what activities the agreement authorizes. An unsigned reseller arrangement is not permission to present as a registered ISO. For each merchant quote, separate interchange and network assessments from processor costs, the merchant-facing markup, and the retained operator share. For each ATM proposal, identify terminal ownership, vault-cash ownership, venue commission, switch fees, replenishment costs, and servicing responsibility. P06 does not authorize splitting one business across unrelated MIDs to escape monitoring; submit the true business model and beneficial owners through the sponsor's process. Document MATCH screening responsibility and the sponsor's current dispute thresholds without inventing a universal safe percentage. P04 and P05 require separate pricing designs: debit restrictions under 15 U.S.C. 1693o-2 do not create a general permission to surcharge debit cards. Require the processor's supported tender logic and jurisdiction-specific price presentation before either play reaches a live terminal. Keep rejected configurations as regression-test cases for every subsequent software update.

On Days 5–7, freeze the launch budget and evidence architecture. The illustrative capital package is $20,000 of unrestricted operating cash plus $5,000 of separately controlled vault cash, a $25,000 startup within the canonical $8,000–$45,000 range. Cap Days 1–30 operating cash deployment at $6,000: $2,000 equipment and installation, $1,000 sponsor and software setup, $1,800 contractor work, $600 travel and prospecting, and $600 contingency. Unused categories remain unspent; a contingency allocation is not a purchasing instruction. Limit Days 31–60 and 61–90 to another $4,000 each, preserving $6,000 operating liquidity before receipts. This cash schedule includes equipment purchases and therefore differs from recurring expense recognition. Vault principal never funds payroll, and merchant settlement balances never enter the operator's budget. Configure IRIS CRM with play ID, sponsor, consented contact source, underwriting status, quoted economics, and next evidence date. Store sensitive boarding documents only in the sponsor-approved intake system; use CRM references rather than copies of identity records. Create a separate ATM ledger linking terminal identifier, venue contract, dispenser balance, settlement receivable, and cash-service ticket. Export weekly evidence before changing any pricing or residual assumptions.

Verify the ATM venue agreement, controlled cash custody, insurance scope, switch activation, and the 12 CFR 1005.16 fee screen with affirmative consumer continuation.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Build a Qualified Pipeline and Prove Installation Readiness
paragraphs: Days 8–10 are a narrow acquisition sprint, not a mass solicitation exercise. Select one merchant vertical the sponsor accepts and one ATM venue archetype with observable cash demand. Build thirty named merchant prospects and ten venue prospects using public business information and introductions. A qualified merchant has an authorized decision-maker, an eligible business model, a documented pricing problem, and willingness to provide a current statement through the approved channel. A qualified venue has a decision-maker, viable power and communications, an accessible placement position, and evidence of cash demand beyond an owner's estimate. Target ten completed merchant discovery conversations and four venue walkthroughs by Day 14; these are internal workload targets, not expected close rates. Use P02 and P03 as the default offer, presenting P04 or P05 only when the merchant's operating environment supports them. Capture the current effective processing cost, transaction count, average ticket, card mix, and recurring gateway charges. Do not compare an interchange-plus quote against a blended headline rate while ignoring per-item costs. For venues, record operating hours, nearby competing ATMs, existing cash-back options, seasonality, and physical access constraints. Photograph the proposed equipment position only with venue permission and exclude customers.

Days 11–12 convert interest into complete, truthful submissions. The boarding contractor checks the sponsor's required identity, ownership, bank-account, website, refund-policy, and fulfillment evidence, while the operator resolves commercial questions. Submit three complete merchant files by Day 14 if the qualified pipeline supports them; never manufacture completeness to meet the target. Record the sponsor's receipt timestamp and distinguish submitted, accepted for review, approved, installed, and first funded transaction. A merchant is not activated merely because IRIS CRM shows a signed application. Higher-risk placement under P06 stays inactive unless the sponsor expressly accepts that actual business model, descriptor, settlement structure, and reserve terms. For P09, ask whether Verifi RDR or Ethoca integration is available through the processor and determine account eligibility, event pricing, duplicate-event handling, and refund authority. Do not assume every alert prevents a dispute or that automation removes chargeback exposure. Configure refund limits and reconcile processor outcomes before expanding automation. The contractor may collect missing records but cannot edit merchant facts to satisfy underwriting. Escalate inconsistencies to the sponsor, record the response, and close the opportunity when the business cannot substantiate its activities. Protecting the upstream relationship outweighs one attractive residual.

Days 13–14 establish ATM site economics and deployment readiness without ordering equipment for an unproven location. Obtain two written venue proposals covering exclusivity, term, commission calculation, access, power, network availability, early termination, equipment removal, and responsibility for damage. Exclusivity must identify its actual scope; a vague promise does not prevent competing cash-back or another terminal elsewhere on the property. Build a downside transaction estimate from observed demand and comparable evidence, then obtain the cash provider's service frequency and minimum charge. Test the ATM fee-disclosure flow required by 12 CFR 1005.16: disclose the fee on screen or paper before commitment and obtain the consumer's election to continue. Do not substitute an exterior sticker for the required transaction-stage disclosure. Evaluate P12 alerts for low cash, offline status, dispenser errors, and tamper events, with named responders and after-hours contact coverage. FinCEN treatment depends on actual activities under 31 CFR 1010.100(ff); a conventional withdrawal ATM is not automatically an MSB solely because it dispenses cash. Expanded transfer or exchange services require a fresh activity assessment. The operator closes Week 2 with a documented readiness decision, not a ceremonial installation deadline.

callout.title: Four Tactics That Preserve Residuals and Avoid Expensive Installations
callout.body: Use contract detail and transaction evidence to improve the pilot before adding prospect volume.
items: Ask for an anonymized sample residual statement before signing Schedule A; locate every fee code and confirm whether gateway revenue shares use a different calculation.
Ask merchants about their latest repricing notice and unresolved support incident; a documented switching reason is stronger qualification than a generic savings promise.
Count venue cash requests during more than one operating period; weekend-only observations can materially overstate weekday withdrawal demand.
Negotiate ATM removal access and commission calculation together; exclusivity has little value when a weak location traps equipment behind an uncooperative counterparty.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Activate Only Approved Accounts and Reconcile Every Dollar
paragraphs: Days 15–17 run controlled activation only where external approvals and contracts are complete. Candidate #32 has a canonical one-to-four-month time to first deal, so a ready pipeline without a live account can still be a valid first-month outcome. Do not force a transaction through an unapproved MID to make the calendar look successful. For each approved merchant, the integration contractor verifies descriptor, terminal identifiers, authorized tender types, refund behavior, receipt content, and funding instructions using the processor's supported test procedures. Test P04 and P05 separately; a cash-discount label does not repair an incorrectly implemented surcharge. Confirm the relevant state rule, including New York General Business Law section 518 where applicable, against the displayed total price. The operator owns the commercial explanation, while the boarding contractor retains evidence of merchant training and support contacts. For an approved ATM location, the field contractor records installation, safe access, communications, fee-screen behavior, and opening cash count with the cash custodian. Perform controlled withdrawal and reversal checks through the approved switch process. Do not store PIN data or full card credentials in tickets. Any cash discrepancy, misleading fee display, or misdirected settlement suspends that installation until corrected.

Days 18–19 separate pilot contribution from the annual scorecard. Consider an illustrative merchant processing $10,000 monthly with a retained twenty-basis-point spread: $10,000 multiplied by 0.002 produces $20, and an $8 retained gateway markup produces $28 operator revenue. With $3 incremental servicing cost, monthly contribution is $25; $150 acquisition spending therefore requires six months of stable contribution to recover. Merchant card sales are not operator revenue. For an illustrative agency-style ATM contract, 200 monthly withdrawals at $3.50 produce $700 customer surcharges. If the contract analysis supports excluding $175 of venue entitlement and $100 of processor entitlement from operator revenue, retained revenue is $425. Deduct $120 cash servicing and $30 maintenance to obtain $275 location contribution before shared overhead. Actual gross-versus-net presentation requires the ASC 606 principal-agent assessment; do not net every cost simply because cash passes through a settlement account. Label these unit examples as planning assumptions until statements validate them. P07 compares expected entitlements with processor reports, while P11 tests whether surcharge changes improve contribution without destroying withdrawals. Count completed, settled withdrawals rather than balance inquiries, reversals, or attempted transactions.

Days 20–21 reconcile the scorecard and operating dashboard without pretending that pilot receipts establish an annual run rate. Formula v2.0 uses $90,000 retained annual operator revenue at a 30% net margin for $27,000 owner profit, leaving $63,000 annual costs. The Base case is $445,000 at 42.5%, producing $189,125 profit and $255,875 costs. The Scaled case is $800,000 at 55%, producing $440,000 profit and $360,000 costs. Although the canonical scorecard labels its revenue field gross revenue, its specified basis here is retained ISO residuals, gateway markups, and ATM surcharges, not merchant settlements or vault principal. Preserve that basis in every comparison. Conservative and Base use one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time staff plus four contractors. Do not attribute the Scaled result to the launch pod. The canonical $1,500–$10,000 monthly operating range is a startup planning reference, not a ceiling on every annual scenario's total costs. Keep launch cash deployment, recurring expenses, direct costs, and capital purchases in separate columns. Track accrued residuals separately from cash received because processor payment timing can leave profitable-looking growth unable to pay next month's contractor invoices.
